description: Small evergreen tree of 3 to 5 metres with thick diamond-shaped leaves, each ending in three sharp spines. It fruits red in late autumn and winter, when almost nothing else does.
nativeStatus: Native to central and northern Argentina and neighbouring countries
nativeRange: Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, Bolivia, southern Brazil
ecology: A tree of the espinal, talares and monte. When young it is hemiparasitic, attaching its roots to neighbouring plants and drawing part of its nutrition from them, so it establishes best near existing shrubs.
wildlifeNotes: The small greenish flowers are plain to look at but very rich in nectar, and the insects they pull in bring insectivorous birds with them. Birds eat the red fruit and spread the seed.
flowering: Small fragrant greenish white flowers in late autumn
fruiting: Red fruit about 1 cm across, in winter
propagation: Plant it near established shrubs. While young it takes part of its nutrition from their roots.
